newsitem.title: USA: CSCE files with CFTC for BFP milk futures contract.
newsitem.headline: CSCE files with CFTC for BFP milk futures contract.

text.p: The New York Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) has filed with the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) for approval for a new milk futures and options contract based on the Basic Formula Price (BFP), the industry benchmark for milk prices, the exchange said Friday.
"The contracts will provide a direct hedging mechanism for dairy firms, and cooperatives and processors who currently price their milk using BFP," CSCE president James Bowe said.

The CSCE already has a milk futures and options contract, launched in December 1995, based on Grade-A milk. Grade-A milk may be used for any purpose, while Grade-B milk is used in manufacturing dairy products, such as butter, cheese and nonfat dry milk.

The CSCE also trades other dairy products, such as nonfat dry milk futures and options and cheddar cheese futures, introduced in 1993, and butter futures and options introduced last month. But the CSCE contracts with the most daily volume are its coffee, sugar and cocoa contracts.
The Chicago Mercantile Exchange also trades milk and butter futures.
The CSCE's new BFP milk futures will be based on the BFP, which is announced monthly by the U.S. Agriculture Department (USDA).
This calculated survey price represents the minimum price for the Federal Milk Marketing Orders and is a benchmark widely used in most segments of the milk industry, Rowe said.
In addition, the price farmers receive for their milk (so called "mailbox prices") is closely related to the BFP.
The CSCE's BFP milk contract will be cash settled and calls for a contract size of 1,000 times the BFP, equivalent to 100,000 pounds of milk.
Trading hours will be 9.00-14.00 EST (13.00-19.00GMT) and the price quotation will in cents per hundredweight.
"The BFP is the basic mover of all milk prices, and everybody in the industry knows what BFP represents," MidAmerica Dairymen Inc, director of statistical analysis, Bill Brooks said.
"By basing this new market of the BFP, the exchange is providing the industry with a very valuable tool to manage price risk," he said.
"We are in the process of developing a forward contract for our members and having a cash settled futures market based on the BFP will help us greatly in the functionality of our contract," he said.

To generate member support and liquidity in the new contract, the CSCE will include the BFP milk futures and options in its existing market maker program, under which three registered market makers serve as catalysts for market activity, providing a bid and offer in the trading ring at all times of the trading day, Rowe said.
